findings.explanation: The analysis selects the three linked components through paths below the root. Separating root layout from the defective recursive source URL is appropriate; physical payload presence in this inspection capture is not the criterion.

Frozen tracked-path identities and native commit history demonstrate version control of text, code and configuration. Capture omissions cannot establish uncommitted deletions in the original object.

The retained annex pointers identify the large image layers by content keys, and raw-data documentation specifies git-annex. The omitted bytes do not negate this tracking mechanism. This does not verify storage access or the contents of those binaries.

The root run explicitly records container/image and output paths, while the label-producing run records ambient Python through compute_all.sh without an exact environment identity. Those label TSVs are used by the root analysis, so the upstream provenance gap is material and partial is supported.

Root installation and usage instructions are real, but the declared boundary includes the label component. Its README instructs execution of preprocessing/detection files absent from the complete pinned inventory, whereas the native result record executes compute_all.sh. This is a documentation-versus-record disagreement under native rule 10, not merely a missing architectural overview. The assessment notes it only under may/002 and still gives an unqualified met here.

The archive contains content-addressed configuration and layer identifiers. The adapter derives and executes the config hash rather than pulling a mutable latest tag. That supports an attempt to recreate this root environment even though archive bytes and recipient retrieval are unverified.

The frozen annex location metadata and clone instructions are publication evidence, not independent retrieval of the image. Not-checked correctly preserves the network/payload restriction rather than turning missing capture bytes into failure or successful access.

findings.explanation: Root, classifier and data modules use Git identities; annex adds content tracking within that system. Separate repositories and two pinned classifier revisions do not imply competing version-control systems.

Classifier CI is defined and historical root execution is recorded, but neither establishes a recurring test series for the current whole study instructions. Not-checked correctly avoids inferring absence from the lack of a root CI file.

Raw inputs and label derivatives have separate component boundaries, and the root code, image definition and outputs occupy distinct paths. The property does not require every directory to be a separate repository.

The documented data policy declares unrestricted access and no restricted component is identified. The host-local source URL establishes poor discoverability, not access control. Empty-subject not-applicable is preferable to a citation-free met; actual access is still unverified.

The exit-zero historical analysis record and adapter docker run --rm mechanism together supply completed fresh-container execution evidence under the method. The answer appropriately limits this to the historical analysis, not a new scientific comparison or proof that the converted current image was rerun.

The root execution creates a disposable Docker container. The linked label-generation record instead invokes bash and ambient Python; its script does not create any disposable environment. The same component is included in must/006, so an unqualified met for each execution overstates the declared scope. Root temporary HOME cleanup also occurs only after success.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the complete linked workflow and retain met as a component-level observation for the root Docker route. Do not describe temporary HOME cleanup as unconditional.

findings.explanation: The retained build and later image conversion are concrete events but not evidence of regular reconstitution testing. Classifier CI installs dependencies without replaying the study image. Not-checked fits the unresolved frequency and exact-environment questions.

Archive layout, content keys and a conversion record show that actual image artifacts are represented within the object. That is stronger than a Dockerfile or registry tag; unavailable bytes in this inspection cohort must remain an access limitation rather than evidence that the original object lacks an archive.

The duplicate answer is consistent with must/014 and correctly flagged. The runnable build/save procedure and later tracked changes satisfy the declared-and-instantiated rule; no separate evidence standard should be invented for the duplicate.

Independent project components are explicitly linked and pinned, while the recursive acquisition source has a host-local URL. Partial is supported under the native rule requiring retrievable component links; ordinary package dependencies are correctly excluded from this modularity criterion.

The machine-readable module map exists, but the human narrative does not reconcile the root classifier with the different classifier revision used for labels or explain the actual label regeneration route. Partial is supported; the missing-script discrepancy deserves an actionability finding as well.

Pinned repositories and file-based TSV interfaces provide independent component boundaries. This is a supported design-level judgment, not a guarantee that arbitrary upgrades preserve API/schema compatibility. The assessment explicitly states that updates were not executed.
Gitlinks compose versions, the registration composes the image with Make, and the recorded inputs select linked datasets. These are concrete composition mechanisms rather than folder names alone.

Named submodule paths/URLs and DataLad commands provide tooling to traverse the structure. The criterion allows tooling, so a missing integrated explanatory map does not force the same status as may/002.
